## Epic A — Reverse-engineer and rebuild ProjectVania (2009 XNA platformer engine) in Unity
- **U.VAN-US-A1 ✅** As the owner, the rules live in an engine-free Core assembly (noEngineReferences, no UnityEngine) that steps at exactly 1/60 s with an accumulator, changes state only through commands carrying a player id that produce events, and is tested with dotnet test outside Unity, with Runtime, Editor and Tests as separate one-way asmdefs, so the original's per-frame arithmetic is copied exactly and presentation never mutates the game (RECONSTRUCTION 0, 1, 2).
- **U.VAN-US-A2 ✅** As the owner, every tuning number, content definition and text is data validated on load behind a settings registry (the player constants of section 4.2, the 16 px grid and the bridge level, the animation table, the menu tree, the camera and console constants, the audio cue table, the segment definitions and the name list), so nothing is a magic number in behaviour and a test proves each file loads (RECONSTRUCTION 4.2, 5, 9, 13).
- **U.VAN-US-A3 ✅** As the owner, the project is a modern Unity 6 setup built in code: URP behind a pipeline-agnostic layer with a pixel-perfect 800x600 reference, the Input System, Unity.Shared profiles and settings, a scripted batch build and test entry point, a trimmed package manifest, and scenes and UI composed by a code-built bootstrap instead of hand-wired Inspector state (RECONSTRUCTION 0).
- **U.VAN-US-A4 ✅** As a player, my keyboard and Xbox pad do exactly what the original's did in each game state (Play, MainMenu, Console, MapEditor): A/D move, S kneels, Space jumps on press, [ and ] or L1/R1 cycle players, Esc/Start the menu, tilde/Back the console, R resets, F12 fullscreen, U the quick bar, C the camera mode, M or middle mouse the editor, the scroll, zoom and rotate keys, and the wheel zoom, with the original's edge and hold semantics (RECONSTRUCTION 3).
- **U.VAN-US-A5 ✅** As a player, the world is the original's 118x75 grid of 16 px cells (Hard, Soft, Empty) with the starting bridge level (a full floor on row 30 and two full-height walls on columns 20 and 40) and the original's floor, ceiling and horizontal collision queries, including the partial-wall rule, proven by Core tests that reproduce the original's cell lookups (RECONSTRUCTION 5).
- **U.VAN-US-A6 ✅** As a player, my character runs to a steady 116 px/s on the ground and 130 px/s in the air, jumps a full fixed curve of about 76 px that releasing the key does not shorten, falls under 10 per frame to 500, kneels on a terminal-speed landing, slides out of a run, wall slides at 83 px/s, wall jumps and drops after one idle second on a wall, all as the original's per-frame state machine, proven by Core tests that replay traced frame sequences (RECONSTRUCTION 4.2-4.7, 4.9).
- **U.VAN-US-A7 ✅** As a player, I see the original's characters animated from their sprite sheets (Morris with idle, run, jump, fall, wall slide, kneel and slide; Shanoa and Leo with idle and run) at the original frame times, drawn at a bottom-centre origin and flipped by facing and wall jump, with a random name from the original name list drawn over each player in red and yellow, and two players of whom [ and ] choose the driven one (RECONSTRUCTION 4.1, 4.8).
- **U.VAN-US-A8 ✅** As a player, I see the painted mountain-farmhouse backdrop at its original size, the white map outline, and every Hard cell drawn from the tileset at its source rectangle, with every cell visible while the editor is open, drawn on the CornflowerBlue clear colour in the original's order of outline, layers, then cells (RECONSTRUCTION 5, 6).
- **U.VAN-US-A9 ✅** As a player, the camera eases toward the current player in Loose mode with the original's 0.02 pull and 0.7 damping, can be locked to the player, follow the editor cursor, or run free (C cycles them), clamps its centre to the map, and responds to the scroll, zoom (scale cubed) and rotate keys and the wheel exactly as the original's (RECONSTRUCTION 7).
- **U.VAN-US-A10 ✅** As a player, Esc opens the original's three-level main menu (Game, Video with Toggle Fullscreen, Audio, Controls, Quit) over a darkened screen with its arrow indicator, titles, descriptions, wrap-around navigation and sounds, the world freezes while it is open, and Quit exits, with the game states Play, MainMenu, Console and MapEditor changing as the table in RECONSTRUCTION 2 says.
- **U.VAN-US-A11 ✅** As a player, the tilde key slides a 200 px console down over the world with its blinking prompt, 100-line history, command recall and typed-key rules, and runs the original's script language (say, yell, fade, play music, play battle, msg hi, exit, version, pause, mute, lee, console clear/full/text/history/bg and the colour parameters) with no crash on a short command (RECONSTRUCTION 10).
- **U.VAN-US-A12 ✅** As a player, the original's HUD is always drawn: the portrait frame and quick bar (U slides it), the falling and fading message stack with its six start-up messages and the gamepad notice, the full-screen fade lens driven by the fade commands, and the debug readout of player, camera, cursor, selected cell and frame rate at the original positions (RECONSTRUCTION 9.1).
- **U.VAN-US-A13 ✅** As a player, I hear the original's sounds from a cue table: the menu and console ambience cues, the run step and wall-slide drag cues (throttled to once per animation frame and per clip), and the two songs started only by the console, with mute and pause working, and the unplayed footstep, step1, jump1 and music1 cues kept in the table (RECONSTRUCTION 11).
- **U.VAN-US-A14 ✅** As a player, M or the middle mouse button opens the map editor: the camera becomes a mouse-look joystick over a cursor, left click paints a Hard cell from the selected palette tile, right click erases it, the highlight tints the cell under the cursor, a player can be dragged with the mouse, and holding Space switches to the palette cursor to pick a tile, with no painting outside the grid (RECONSTRUCTION 8, 12).
- **U.VAN-US-A15 ✅** As a player, the world draws through the original's filter effect (a mild vignette) and the other four shaders (bloom, negative, pause, water) exist as selectable post-process presets that nothing enables, as in the original (RECONSTRUCTION 6.1).
- **U.VAN-US-A16 ✅** As the owner, everything the original built but never wired is kept as data and inert behaviour (the eleven segment definitions and the segment atlas, the 16 ledge slots, the Sun day-night cycle, the action cross, the seven portraits, the skill icons, the five area layers, the particle, selector, banner and sprite-sheet art, the Shanoa, Leo and Richter art), so the rebuild loses nothing the original contained (RECONSTRUCTION 5.1, 9.1, 13, 15).
- **U.VAN-US-A17 ✅** As the owner, every sprite, texture, sound, font and data file the original loaded is in the rebuild, proven by a test that diffs the original's live asset list (RECONSTRUCTION 13) against the rebuild's content registry, with the poisondart and consecrate icons imported as their own files.
- **U.VAN-US-A18 ✅** As the owner, the finished game is verified end to end by a scripted run that plays every state and mechanic of the original (run, jump, kneel, slide, wall slide, wall jump, camera modes, menu, console commands, editor painting, audio) and captures screenshots, settles the two kept-pending behaviours (kneel release, wall jump push-off), and compares them with RECONSTRUCTION, so the repo can be called a complete proof of concept of the original.
